title: An Unexpected Tetragonal Network of Seven-Connected Er6 Clusters Stabilized by Multiple Halogen Bonds through Cooperative Effects

material_class.structural_family: carbonate-bridged trigonal-prismatic Er6 cluster; hydrogen-bonded dimers

synthesis.procedure: Under ambient air, H2oepch (0.15 mmol) was dissolved in 10 mL MeOH/DCM (1:2) and triethylamine (0.4 mmol) was added. A separately prepared solution of ErCl3·6H2O (0.15 mmol) in 5 mL MeOH/DCM (1:2) was added dropwise, giving an immediate color change from yellow to dark orange. The mixture was stirred for 16 h at room temperature, filtered, and left undisturbed for slow evaporation. Orange X-ray-quality crystals formed after 14 days. The two μ-carbonates arise from aerial CO2 fixation. The ligand H2oepch was obtained in 90% yield by a literature procedure.
synthesis.time: 16 h stirring, then 14 days slow evaporation
synthesis.vessel_or_method: ambient air; stirred solution followed by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration and undisturbed slow evaporation to orange crystals

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT is close to six uncoupled Er(III) ions and falls on cooling; Curie–Weiss analysis indicates antiferromagnetic coupling. Magnetization is unsaturated at 7 T and reduced-magnetization curves do not superimpose, consistent with significant anisotropy. No out-of-phase ac signal and therefore no SMM behavior above 2 K.

source_locations.location: Table S1 and experimental formula for (1)

material_class.structural_family: carbonate-bridged trigonal-prismatic Er6 cluster assembled by Br···Br halogen bonds into a 7-connected supramolecular tetragonal network

synthesis.procedure: The procedure used for compound 1 was repeated under ambient air with H2opch-Br (0.15 mmol) in place of H2oepch: the ligand in 10 mL MeOH/DCM (1:2) was treated with triethylamine (0.4 mmol), ErCl3·6H2O (0.15 mmol) in 5 mL MeOH/DCM (1:2) was added dropwise, and the dark-orange mixture was stirred for 16 h at room temperature, filtered, and crystallized by slow evaporation. Orange X-ray-quality crystals were obtained. The μ-carbonates arise from aerial CO2 fixation. H2opch-Br was prepared from pyrazine-2-carbohydrazide (10 mmol) in 25 mL water and 5-bromo-2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde (12 mmol) in 50 mL EtOH, stirred 24 h at room temperature, filtered, and washed with cold Et2O (93% yield).
synthesis.vessel_or_method: ambient air; same stirred MeOH/DCM procedure as compound 1, then slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration and slow evaporation to orange crystals

properties.summary: Magnetic behavior is essentially identical to compound 1: χMT is near the value for six uncoupled Er(III) ions and decreases on cooling, with a negative Weiss constant indicating antiferromagnetic coupling. Magnetization is unsaturated at 7 T and shows anisotropy. No ac out-of-phase signal is observed, so there is no SMM behavior above 2 K; the halogen-bond network does not provide a significant intermolecular magnetic pathway.

source_locations.location: Table S1 and experimental formula for (2)
